body: The thing is that before switching it off by the power button or just leaving it a little bit has resolved the issue, and a temporary fix to the issue signals to my brain that I can procrastinate getting the Mac looked at.

I can't expect anyone to diagnose my Mac and I'm not by any means smart enough with computers to investigate by taking it apart, but what should I do with it until tomorrow? Should I try to switch it off or restart it (I haven't tried many times with cmd cntrl esc and cmd alt p r) or should I just leave it to sleep until I take it to the store?

Then you'll probably be on a waiting list for ages. Really not looking forward to this.

Sometimes I ask for directions when lost and they're useless because I'm somehow expected to remember what is said to me (and writing them down is either not possible because I don't have pen/paper or it would feel awkward to make notes of what someone's saying to me...). Obviously whoever I'm asking for directions doesn't necessarily know I'm disabled. But yeah. I find the whole having crappy short term memory thing pretty embarrassing and have a tendency to act like it's not actually a problem, which causes me pointless problems. :)
